label: Friday, November 6, 2026 · Dip-buyers edition
intro: Thursday was the crash after the blue-wave party: the Nasdaq fell 5.5 percent, its worst day since 2020, and the Nasdaq slipped back into a correction. Friday the dip buyers showed up as the October jobs report beat forecasts, and chip stocks led the rebound.

items.title: Dip buyers emerge as chipmakers rally after the selloff
items.take: Friday opened with the Nasdaq 100 up 2% and a gauge of chip giants up 6% as dip buyers returned. But the solid jobs reading reinforced bets the Fed will hike rates again in December, and short-dated Treasuries underperformed.

items.title: Nasdaq, S&P rebound after brutal sell-off as US adds 165K jobs
items.take: The October jobs report beat every forecast: 165,000 jobs added, versus 65,000 expected and a revised 60,000 in September. Chip stocks bounced after their worst sell-off since 2020, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index up 4% after Thursday's 12% plunge and Intel up 6%.

items.title: US tech stocks open higher after worst day in 19 months
items.take: Thursday's rout was the real story: Nasdaq down 5.5%, Dow down 1,833 points, S&P down 4.4% as investors exited AI positions en masse. Friday's bounce is partial, the Dow was still down about 1% at the open, and copper is on track for its biggest weekly drop since March.

items.title: Rate-hike odds settle as jobless claims hit a 57-year low
items.take: Weekly jobless claims matched a 57-year low of 189,000, and money markets scaled back December rate-hike odds to about 65% from over 80%. Elsewhere Airbnb jumped 12% on a raised forecast and Goldman cut its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150 on the hawkish Fed outlook.

items.title: Stocks tumble steeply as markets weigh future of AI build-out
items.take: The Post frames Thursday's slide as the market repricing the AI build-out itself, wiping out the post-midterm gains in a single session. With a companion piece noting the US remains vulnerable to oil shocks 50 years on, the macro picture is doing no favors for risk appetite.

items.title: Podcast: Instant Reaction — US adds 165,000 jobs, topping all forecasts
items.take: This week's rotation pick is the fastest take on the number everyone is chewing on: Bloomberg Surveillance's instant reaction to the October jobs report, out this morning.
